name: OpenHuman v0.64.15
body:
# The Installed-Build Reliability Upgrade

This release focuses on keeping installed apps rock-solid—especially when loading key modules like search and memory. Onward and upward! 🎉

## Highlights

### Modules & installed builds 🧩
A targeted hotfix improves module admission in installed builds so critical modules load correctly again—unblocking both search (`tinysearch`) and memory (`tinymemory`) where they could previously fail due to module directory permission checks.  

([#7155](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7155)) — Thank you @senamakel!

## Contributor Credits
Thanks to @senamakel for the fix and the fast turnaround!

name: OpenHuman v0.64.14
body:
# The Files, Memory & Voice Power-Up

This release is a big step forward in day-to-day usability: clearer files and sessions, a major memory evolution, and real-time voice agents—plus a ton of reliability and performance work across the stack. 🎉

## Highlights

### Files & project workspace clarity 🗂️
Agent outputs now land in a visible **Files** folder, you can choose where that folder lives, and the app can surface those generated files directly in-place—making it much easier to find and use what your agent created. Large tool outputs are also handled more safely to keep projects tidy. ([#6820](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6820), [#6825](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6825), [#6833](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6833), [#6868](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6868), [#6947](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6947)) — Thank you @M3gA-Mind and @senamakel!

### Memory v2, imports, and safer organization 🧠
Memory gets a major upgrade: **engine-selectable memory v2**, better lifecycle handling around each turn, and stronger portability when switching engines. The Memory UI and provider cards were modernized (including CortexDB), credits/free-period behavior is more consistent (with top-up prompts), and recall becomes time-zone aware.

Imports and migrations are significantly hardened: clearer “building vs empty” states, smarter batching/retries, better failure visibility with retry controls, more reliable resuming, and improved document ingestion (PDF/Office). Organization also improves with connector-first filing, better GitHub scoping, optional attribution to senders, and multiple erasure/deletion correctness and privacy/security fixes. ([#6841](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6841), [#6843](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6843), [#6855](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6855), ### Live voice agents & voice foundations 🎙️
Voice agents are now truly live: talk to Tiny in real time with tool support (including Gemini Live, ElevenLabs, and Sarvam), plus a redesigned Voice agents experience with service cards, settings modals, and app-wide toasts. Under the hood, voice-related inference components were also reorganized for a cleaner foundation. ([#7046](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7046), [#7092](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7092), [#6840](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6840)) — Thank you @senamakel!

### Chat UX upgrades & smoother conversation control 💬
Chat gets a substantial UI uplift: working folder support, per-model thinking controls, real thread titles, richer sidebar context, and clearer run-state cues. Reliability improves too—Stop is more resilient, streaming works even without a progress sink, reply-language directives are consistently sent, and several web chat delivery edge cases are fixed. The app also adds translatable error copy and improves transcript storage formats. ([#7048](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7048), [#7045](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7045), [#6916](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6916), [#7088](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7088), [#7097](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7097), [#7098](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7098), [#6844](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6844), [#7087](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7087), [#6881](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6881), [#6883](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6883)) — Thank you @senamakel and @M3gA-Mind!

### Agent intelligence, tool governance, and turn reliability 🧰
Agents are more robust and predictable: improved tool calling defaults (JSON auto) with a setting, better “finish” verification, fewer false failure classifications, clearer file-read behavior, and multiple fixes around context compaction, reasoning bounds, iteration caps, and hosted-path correctness/telemetry. Tool policy/approval gates were reworked, per-turn tool withholding was added, and timed-out commands now terminate their whole process group.

This also includes targeted fixes for web research budgets, credential scrubber behavior (including avoiding code redaction), handling HTTP status correctly, and improved orchestration behaviors. ([#6910](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6910), [#6909](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6909), [#6963](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6963), [#6965](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6965), [#6966](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6966), [#6967](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6967), [#6968](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6968), [#6969](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6969), [#6971](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6971), [#6972](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6972), [#6973](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6973), [#6974](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6974), [#6975](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6975), [#6976](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6976), [#6977](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6977), [#6980](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6980), [#6992](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6992), [#6889](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6889), [#6856](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6856), [#6879](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6879), [#6884](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6884), [#6945](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6945), [#6946](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6946), [#7117](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7117), [#7118](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7118), [#7119](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7119), [#7120](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7120), [#7140](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7140), [#6865](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6865)) — Thank you @senamakel and @sanil-23!

### Sessions, scheduling, connectors & integrations 🧩
A new host-injected session store moves per-agent conversations outside the workspace, with follow-ups to ensure clean recovery and slot ownership. Scheduled (cron) runs can now deliver output back to the conversation that requested it. Composio and connectors were streamlined with direct-read paths, module routing improvements, and a configurable disabled mode—plus a deliberate removal of Composio→memory sync as memory evolves. ([#7044](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7044), [#7052](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7052), [#7049](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7049), [#6831](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6831), [#6885](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6885), [#6897](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6897), [#6920](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6920)) — Thank you @senamakel!

### Sandbox, Windows, and platform robustness 🛠️
The Docker sandbox flow was reworked, local jail output is captured outside the project, and sandbox capability reporting and host switches are improved (including `OPENHUMAN_SANDBOX=off`). Windows sees key stability fixes around permission-state normalization and environment forwarding into sandboxed children. TinyComputer browser tasks are now runnable from the app, with additional improvements to reuse what completed tasks learned. ([#6862](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6862), [#6970](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6970), [#6981](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6981), [#6988](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6988), [#6847](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6847), [#6998](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6998), [#7008](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7008), [#7127](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7127)) — Thank you @senamakel, @ajabaabaa, and @YellowSnnowmann!

### Models, routing, search, and local AI direction 🧭
Routing and model selection were tightened across the UI and composer, including honoring provider picks and avoiding offering models/search tools that a session or offline profile can’t use. The tool-search path is expanded beyond the TinyHumans proxy, thinking-level controls are passed through to providers, and uploads are persisted with a preference for native multimodal input.

The local AI story is also simplified: in-app model downloads and Ollama lifecycle management were removed, while continuing to support local inference via user-run endpoints. ([#6978](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6978), [#6996](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6996), [#7004](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7004), [#7026](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7026), [#6908](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6908), [#6911](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6911), [#6987](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6987), [#6858](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6858)) — Thank you @SayrWolfridge, @sx4im, @obchain, and @senamakel!

### Internationalization & onboarding polish 🌍
New locales landed (Japanese and Turkish), Arabic translations were improved with added Arabic README docs, and the overall translation catalog was significantly pruned for maintainability. Onboarding is also shorter and more accurate for the local path. ([#6986](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6986), [#7039](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7039), [#7024](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7024), [#6860](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6860), [#7009](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/7009)) — Thank you @tjm8874, @moersoy, @taljeri, @graycyrus, and @senamakel!

### Release engineering, CI health, and build performance 🚀
This range includes a massive internal modernization: waves of refactors moving functionality into shared “tiny*” libraries, vendor pin hygiene, and major dead-code/dependency pruning. CI and tests were stabilized (including clippy/layout gates), redundant tests were removed or consolidated, and performance improvements landed for both runtime and build outputs (including module bundling at build time on every platform).

Release-specific work also improved macOS notarization of module bundles (with signature verification and tests), and headless deployments gained better keyring support. Benchmark tooling and docs expanded substantially, including a cross-harness rig and supporting runbooks and viewers. name: OpenHuman v0.64.10
body:
# The Speed, Structure & Reliability Upgrade

This release tightens the core experience from end to end—faster first turns, clearer chat feedback, sturdier integrations, and a big internal modularity push that sets us up for even quicker iteration. 🎉

## Highlights

### Performance & responsiveness ⚡
The agent loop is noticeably snappier: first-turn prompts are dramatically smaller, prompt caching stays warm (improving time-to-first-token), and the managed inference path avoids unnecessary per-call client setup. Tool-output compaction is also enabled by default again—with new “REPL-style” tools over stored results to keep large tool outputs from stalling turns.

([#6787](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6787), [#6788](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6788), [#6823](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6823)) — Thank you @senamakel!

### Chat UI & approvals polish 💬
Chat got a round of UX improvements: long source lists now collapse cleanly (with better favicons), web-search rendering no longer leaves awkward gaps, and the silence watchdog now warns instead of killing a running turn—staying in sync with the core’s actual turn state. Approvals are also smoother: answered approvals won’t “ghost” into the background deck, and refusals now carry a clear deny reason that the model can actually read.

([#6802](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6802), [#6827](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6827), [#6800](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6800), [#6810](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6810)) — Thank you @senamakel and @M3gA-Mind!

### Memory & knowledge engines 🧠
Memory is now explicitly selectable: you can choose exactly one active engine, including Local (TinyCortex) or CortexDB via TinyHumans, plus other supported providers. Switching engines can also copy existing memories across—making experimentation and migration much less painful.

([#6777](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6777)) — Thank you @senamakel!

### MCP & Composio integrations 🔌
MCP tooling becomes much more ergonomic and robust: server tools are exposed as stable, individually-addressable tools from a persistent cache, and string-encoded JSON arguments are normalized so calls don’t fail unexpectedly. Refusals from tool listing now tell the model what it *can* do (and avoid pointing at RPC-only methods). On the Composio side, embedders can give each agent its own credentials, and backend-routed Composio calls now flow through the tinyconnectors module instead of an in-process client.

([#6767](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6767), [#6769](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6769), [#6818](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6818), [#6689](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6689), [#6796](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6796)) — Thank you @senamakel, @M3gA-Mind, and @oxoxDev!

### Security, safety & policy hardening 🛡️
Security protections are sharper and less noisy: the prompt-injection guard is less likely to false-positive on recalled transcripts, and browser IP blocking now uses the full non-global range definitions (with regression tests). Shell execution reliability also improves in scheduled jobs on Windows, and shell scanning logic is consolidated upstream for consistency.

([#6776](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6776), [#6709](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6709), [#6764](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6764), [#6790](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6790)) — Thank you @senamakel, @Avi-Bendetsky, and @sanil-23!

### Architecture & vendor modularity push 🧱
A major theme of this series is extracting host-independent logic out of `openhuman-core` and into the appropriate `vendor/tiny*` modules—keeping core focused on product policy, adapters, and contracts. This includes splitting RPC/server responsibilities, moving channels/skills/web3/filesystem/hooks/session/runtime/tooling helpers into their owning crates, and updating vendor pins to merged upstream mains. Along the way, stale subsystem references were cleaned up, and the tool-call type is now adopted directly from tinytools to reduce duplication and drift.

([#6703](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6703), [#6779](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6779), [#6780](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6780), [#6782](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6782), [#6783](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6783), [#6784](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6784), [#6785](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6785), [#6786](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6786), [#6789](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6789), [#6791](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6791), [#6793](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6793), [#6794](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6794), [#6795](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6795), [#6797](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6797), [#6804](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6804), [#6805](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6805), [#6806](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6806), [#6807](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6807), [#6809](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6809), [#6773](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6773)) — Thank you @senamakel!

### Reliability, updates & CI/e2e stability ✅
This set also focuses on “keeping main green”: E2E web runs now avoid port collisions and refuse taken ports, the core updater once again resolves the correct versioned archive and stages the real binary, and managed backend outages now trigger bounded exponential backoff with explicit terminal outcomes. CI coverage improves too, including executing module-gated Rust tests, better layout gating behavior, and keeping vendor/lockfile pins aligned (including tinymcp and tinymemory pin handling).

([#6719](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6719), [#6770](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6770), [#6569](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6569), [#6605](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6605), [#6817](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6817), [#6771](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6771), [#6772](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6772), [#6798](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6798)) — Thank you @obchain, @lorenzozanee, @M3gA-Mind, @sanil-23, and @senamakel!

### Desktop, voice & platform fixes 🖥️
TinyComputer gains saved flows, task reports, and a live Bali booking E2E to make real-world debugging and iteration much easier. There are also key platform fixes: macOS desktop builds were restored after upstream accessibility API changes, and vendor bumps include a Windows build fix for `unsafe_code` constraints in tinyagents.

([#6761](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6761), [#6822](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6822), [#6839](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6839)) — Thank you @senamakel and @M3gA-Mind!

### Web3 & x402 improvements 💱
Web3 functionality continues its move into tinywallet, with follow-on pinning to pick up important x402, fee, probing, and chain-status fixes—plus host-side support and tests to keep behavior correct and traceable.

([#6792](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6792)) — Thank you @senamakel!

### Usage & accounting accuracy 📊
The Usage page now reflects the spend it actually recorded: workspace tracking is fixed across auth transitions, duplicate recordings are avoided (and legacy duplicates ignored), and tiny UI details like `<$0.01` and negative-zero rendering are corrected. The “Token & Cost” tab was also renamed to “Token savings” in all locales to match what it truly shows.

([#6720](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6720)) — Thank you @graycyrus!

### Embedder & agent control knobs 🎛️
Embedders now have tighter control over runs with a per-turn tool-call budget limiter, without needing to alter persistent agent configuration. There’s also cleanup after the inline-skills/deferred-tools work: vestigial spawn args are removed and e2e tests fixed accordingly.

([#6350](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6350), [#6762](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6762)) — Thank you @theamazinghenk and @senamakel!

### Settings & provider catalog changes 🔁
A built-in Cheaper Inference provider entry was added, then reverted—returning settings and documentation to their prior routing behavior.

([#6620](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6620), [#6778](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6778)) — Thank you @aiapienthusiast and @senamakel!

### Docs & developer workflow helpers 🧰
Internal contributor tooling improves with a new tracked Claude skill guide for migrating code into vendor submodules, and tinyskills is bumped to fix sourceUrl resolution behavior for non-`SKILL.md` Markdown blobs.

([#6775](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6775), [#6819](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6819)) — Thank you @senamakel and @M3gA-Mind!

### Release housekeeping 🚀
This range includes the release PR used to cut and ship the bundle.

([#6826](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6826)) — Thank you @M3gA-Mind!
### Additional highlights 🔗

A few more focused contributions round out this release with targeted fixes and improvements that are worth calling out. ([#6781](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6781), [#6803](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6803)) — Thank you @senamakel!

## Contributor Credits

Thanks to everyone who contributed to this release: @aiapienthusiast, @Avi-Bendetsky, @graycyrus, @lorenzozanee, @M3gA-Mind, @obchain, @oxoxDev, @sanil-23, @senamakel, and @theamazinghenk.

# The Better Windows Desktop Upgrade

This release is all about making the Windows desktop experience more reliable, more polished, and smoother to operate—especially when you’re offline. 🎉

## Highlights

### Offline-ready Windows installers 📦
Windows desktop installers now bundle all registry-pinned native modules (and their extracted DLLs) directly into the installer, so key features don’t depend on a first-run download. Module resolution now prefers the read-only installer bundle before user cache or network, and the Windows checks/smoke steps were updated to verify offline module loading end-to-end. ([#6687](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6687)) — Thank you @senamakel!

### Sharper Windows window controls & cleaner shutdown 🪟
Windows gets a more compact first-launch window and improved custom window controls (minimize, maximize/restore, close), with the drag strip staying available during boot and error screens. Shutdown behavior is also fixed so closing properly exits both the desktop host and embedded core (including support for the `app_quit` IPC command), plus the dev launcher was simplified with earlier architecture mismatch detection. ([#6692](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6692)) — Thank you @stevent95-star!

## Contributor Credits
Thanks to everyone who contributed to this release: @senamakel, @stevent95-star.

name: OpenHuman v0.64.3
body:
# The Reliability & Speed Upgrade

v0.64.0 → v0.64.3 is all about making OpenHuman feel steadier under real workloads—fewer loops, better recovery, faster turn startup, and clearer billing/usage surfaces. Ship it. 🚀

## Highlights

### Agent stability & loop control 🧭
Agents now stay focused on the *latest* user request (even after tool search results arrive), avoid getting pulled back into earlier greetings, and stop unproductive tool loops sooner with smarter failure classification and bounded exploration. The result: fewer stalls, fewer repeat calls, and more deterministic “partial-but-useful” outcomes when tools are blocked. ([#6656](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6656), [#6660](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6660), [#6661](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6661)) — Thank you @senamakel!

### Chat recovery, streaming resilience & warm-session correctness 🛠️
This release hardens the chat experience: warm-session completions now properly finalize progress and can optionally capture full successful inference SSE responses for debugging; completed model streams that return no answer get a bounded one-time retry; and transcript/app-state recovery is more robust after failed or torn writes—preserving history and keeping queued follow-ups stable. ([#6665](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6665), [#6685](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6685), [#6686](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6686)) — Thank you @senamakel!

### Faster integrations & skill discovery 🔥
Turn startup and tool availability should feel snappier thanks to caching and warming of Composio integrations and skill metadata across turns/sessions (with clear invalidation rules). This also forwards Socket.IO WebSocket upgrades through the local inference capture proxy for more consistent event routing. ([#6684](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6684)) — Thank you @senamakel!

### Time, time zones & scheduling correctness 🕒
OpenHuman now understands more natural time phrases (like “tomorrow 9am”, “since Monday”, and “in 2h30m”), and Composio connector calls include the user’s IANA time zone—helping downstream results (like Gmail timestamps) line up with what users actually mean. Durable subagents also resume more reliably when session IDs show up in multiple fields. ([#6670](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6670), [#6673](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6673), [#6674](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6674)) — Thank you @senamakel and @M3gA-Mind!

### Observability & developer telemetry 📡
Production Langfuse tracing is enabled from the canonical production API host (while keeping unknown hosts closed), and child agent turns are grouped cleanly under parent conversation lineage—with more complete generation metadata and careful accounting to avoid double counting. ([#6677](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6677)) — Thank you @senamakel!

### Clearer billing & usage UI 💳
Usage and billing surfaces got a reality check: “Usage & Limits” is now “Usage” (removing misleading local budget gauges), provider-call usage logging has a dedicated tab with better filters and bounded record semantics, and billing access is consolidated under Accounts with a hosted dashboard link (with `/settings/billing` preserved as a redirect). Also, chat no longer incorrectly blames empty model responses on insufficient credits—credit guidance now appears only for explicit billing errors. ([#6657](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6657), [#6679](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6679)) — Thank you @senamakel!

### Tooling & platform cleanup (Windows + retired components) 🧹
Windows users should see more reliable TinyMemory module loading thanks to a pinned TinyBus ACL fix, and the retired Medulla integration has been fully removed (while preserving a legacy config alias so older configs load safely as `local`). The orchestrator tool surface was also tightened by removing unused prompt tools and delegate entries. Finally, `file_read` is now unpacked so the orchestrator can read result previews without opening up the whole files tool pack. ([#6680](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6680), [#6682](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6682), [#6669](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6669), [#6666](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6666)) — Thank you @senamakel and @M3gA-Mind!

### Test coverage & regressions ✅
New regression coverage locks in the “greeting → deferred Gmail tool continuation” behavior end-to-end, helping ensure the agent keeps the active request and tool result together and doesn’t fall back into earlier context. ([#6659](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/6659)) — Thank you @senamakel!

## Contributor Credits

Big thanks to everyone who shipped v0.64.0 → v0.64.3: @senamakel, @M3gA-Mind.

# OpenHuman v0.63.11

**187 commits — 52 features, 90 fixes, 45 refactors, docs and CI.** This release carries everything merged to `main` since v0.63.9, including the kernel restructure, ElevenLabs Voice Agents, and a large reliability pass across memory, inference and voice.

> **Note on the previous notes:** an earlier version of this page listed only the two release-promotion PRs. That was an artefact of how `release` is updated, not a description of the release. The full contents are below.

## Highlights

### Voice
- **ElevenLabs Voice Agents** — core RPC, realtime session, and local-agent relay handler ([#5407](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5407))
- Send the relay identity token where the backend can read it ([#5428](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5428))
- Stop the Piper voice id leaking into non-Piper TTS providers ([#5367](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5367))
- Repair the execute bit on extracted Piper binaries ([#5216](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5216)), handle U16 sample format in the fallback capture path ([#4537](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4537))

### Memory & embeddings
- **Warn before the embedding budget silently stops memory** ([#5402](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5402))
- Stop a signed-in user's embeddings failing, and unstick the parked queue ([#5427](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5427))
- Classify Ollama-unavailable embed failures actionably ([#5398](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5398))
- Drain the coding-session backlog across bounded passes ([#5368](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5368))
- Canonicalize memory identifiers symmetrically ([#5275](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5275)); stop paging on caller ingest-payload schema errors ([#5280](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5280))

### Inference & model routing
- Route Codex OAuth chat to the subscription backend ([#5371](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5371))
- Error on a misconfigured vision model instead of substituting ([#5262](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5262)); route vision at vision-capable models ([#5253](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5253))
- Explain background-role provider fallback and verify BYOK keys ([#5254](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5254))
- Route local AI through TinyAgents RPC ([#5240](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5240)); local model reliability — `/api/tags` fallback and real Ollama model ids ([#5219](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5219))

### Flows
- Surface bounded loops from the tinyflows engine ([#5366](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5366))
- Accept declared workflow inputs on every run path ([#5304](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5304))
- Per-item fan-out — run an array of flow work concurrently ([#5302](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5302))
- Canvas visual refresh — kind tiles, elevation, step numbers ([#5303](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5303))

### Agent & chat
- Send user image attachments as image blocks, not text ([#5370](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5370))
- Preserve chat context across a Quick/Reasoning switch ([#5401](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5401))
- Name a thread in three words ([#5412](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5412))
- Name the chat-template rejection instead of blaming model/temperature ([#5309](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5309))
- Filesystem-offload convention for worker artifacts on long-horizon tasks ([#5217](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5217))

### Kernel restructure
- **Collapse 124 flat domains into 31 gate-aligned families** ([#5328](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5328)) — pure moves, byte-identical wire surface
- Kernelize openhuman: cut the workflow dependency floor 418 → 280 crates ([#5314](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5314))
- Realign `DomainGroup` with the family directories ([#5332](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5332)) and guard three unenforced consumers ([#5364](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5364))
- Gate the macOS Contacts cohort behind `contacts` ([#5365](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5365)); host capability adapters and config seam ([#5396](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5396))

### Media, mascot & config
- Error instead of false success on the generation poll timeout ([#5411](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5411))
- Accept PNG/GIF/JPEG/WebP custom avatars with file upload ([#5420](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5420))
- Surface a user notice when a corrupt `config.toml` is reset ([#5340](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5340)); stop transient `active_user.toml` read faults from resetting the profile ([#5337](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5337))

### Channels & sessions
- Stop a missing edit route from looking like a deleted message ([#5283](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5283))
- Keep the `/auth/me` 401 classifiable as session expiry rather than a hard logout ([#5311](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5311))
- Stop out-of-credits background scouts paging Sentry ([#5310](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5310))

# The Flows, Memory, and Voice Power‑Up

This release is packed with deep workflow-building upgrades, a leaner kernelized core, and big reliability wins across memory, inference, and voice—plus a bunch of UI polish that makes everything feel snappier and sturdier. 🎉

## Highlights

### Flows & Workflow Copilot, leveled up 🧩
Workflow authoring and Copilot got a major usability and reliability pass: clearer step labels, a “Save & enable” path, safe live test-runs behind approvals, a Stop button, better run-rail behavior, improved compile/runtime correctness, and a visual refresh across the canvas. There’s also more robust store behavior (corrupt-row handling, transactional upserts), better localization coverage, and tighter run/approval boundaries so what you approve is what runs.

([#5088](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5088), [#5089](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5089), [#5090](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5090), [#5097](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5097), [#5099](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5099), [#5111](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5111), [#5112](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5112), [#5114](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5114), [#5115](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5115), [#5120](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5120), [#5128](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5128), [#5135](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5135), [#5148](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5148), [#5150](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5150), [#5153](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5153), [#5176](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5176), [#5205](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5205), [#5212](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5212), [#5223](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5223), [#5227](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5227), [#5228](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5228), [#5248](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5248), [#5264](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5264), [#5265](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5265), [#5285](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5285), [#5286](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5286), [#5287](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5287), [#5289](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5289), [#5290](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5290), [#5292](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5292), [#5293](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5293), [#5294](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5294), [#5296](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5296), [#5297](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5297), [#5302](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5302), [#5303](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5303), [#5304](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5304), [#5366](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5366)) — Thank you @graycyrus and @senamakel!

### Memory & agent profiles that scale 🧠
Memory took a big step forward: TinyCortex consolidation and tool-memory cutovers continue, identifiers are normalized more reliably, and a new warning helps prevent “silent” memory stoppage when embedding budgets are exhausted. Flows also gained more intentional memory behaviors (flow namespaces + digest, dedicated memory node support, and read-only memory helpers), while profiles gained “hermes-style” homes that neatly organize per-profile workspace, memory, skills, and cron attribution.

([#5043](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5043), [#5101](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5101), [#5118](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5118), [#5140](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5140), [#5175](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5175), [#5176](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5176), [#5205](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5205), [#5220](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5220), [#5227](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5227), [#5237](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5237), [#5244](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5244), [#5246](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5246), [#5275](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5275), [#5280](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5280), [#5282](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5282), [#5368](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5368), [#5398](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5398), [#5402](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5402), [#5427](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5427)) — Thank you @senamakel, @graycyrus, @YellowSnnowmann, @CodeGhost21, and @mysma-9403!

### Voice, mascot, and realtime experiences 🎙️
Voice capture and TTS reliability improved (including better sample-format handling, Piper binary fixes, and cleaner provider behavior), and realtime voice mode is now surfaced by default. There’s also a big new integration: ElevenLabs Voice Agents with core RPC, realtime sessions, and a local relay handler—paired with UX improvements like sentence-by-sentence streaming to reduce perceived delay.

([#4537](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4537), [#5216](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5216), [#5367](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5367), [#5404](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5404), [#5407](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5407), [#5428](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5428), [#5441](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5441)) — Thank you @mysma-9403 and @YellowSnnowmann!

### Chat, conversations, and day-to-day UI polish 💬
Chat and conversation UX got smoother and sturdier: long URLs now wrap correctly, a render loop was fixed, template rejections are clearer, and the thread-goal footer no longer auto-scrolls unexpectedly. The “Human” experience also evolves: the mascot can now live docked inside chat, supports uploaded custom avatars, and avoids lipsync-related UI lockups—plus you can name a thread in three words.

([#5030](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5030), [#5210](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5210), [#5274](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5274), [#5309](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5309), [#5369](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5369), [#5412](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5412), [#5419](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5419), [#5420](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5420)) — Thank you @jgentes, @graycyrus, and @YellowSnnowmann!

### Inference, embeddings, search & cost correctness ⚡
Inference and embeddings behavior is more predictable and safer: better model routing (including vision-capable models), more actionable errors (and redacted secrets), improved local model reliability, and clearer handling for BYOK keys and budgets. Search expands with Exa support (managed + BYOK), and attribution is improved so usage is correctly linked to resolved providers.

([#4885](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4885), [#5103](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5103), [#5117](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5117), [#5206](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5206), [#5207](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5207), [#5215](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5215), [#5218](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5218), [#5219](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5219), [#5222](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5222), [#5253](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5253), [#5254](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5254), [#5262](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5262), [#5363](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5363), [#5371](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5371)) — Thank you @M3gA-Mind, @YellowSnnowmann, and @samrusani!

### Core kernelization, feature gates, and performance 🧱
The core continues getting leaner and more modular: big dependency trimming, kernelization work, DomainGroup realignment, and more functionality gated behind explicit compile-time features. Performance and orchestration also improved with batching, shared config arcs, checkpoint/resume for delegations, and runtime process pooling across agents and skill runs.

([#5029](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5029), [#5040](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5040), [#5052](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5052), [#5061](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5061), [#5062](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5062), [#5068](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5068), [#5078](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5078), [#5079](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5079), [#5129](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5129), [#5178](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5178), [#5202](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5202), [#5233](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5233), [#5240](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5240), [#5314](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5314), [#5328](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5328), [#5332](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5332), [#5364](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5364), [#5365](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5365), [#5396](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5396), [#5405](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5405)) — Thank you @senamakel, @YellowSnnowmann, @oxoxDev, and @mysma-9403!

### Agents, approvals, and orchestration safety 🤖
Agents and approvals got sharper edges removed: replacement routes are preserved during cleanup, path scrubbing is safer, an opt-in “auto-approve-all” setting is available, and custom registry agents now run with their real tools. Orchestration reliability improves in several places too, including cron correctness, removing dead hosted-steering polling, and making delegation/agent behaviors fail loud instead of silently dropping results.

([#4786](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4786), [#4998](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4998), [#5039](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5039), [#5042](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5042), [#5094](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5094), [#5121](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5121), [#5123](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5123), [#5211](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5211), [#5306](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5306)) — Thank you @graycyrus, @samrusani, @mysma-9403, @oxoxDev, @sanil-23, and @M3gA-Mind!

### Desktop packaging, config/auth resilience & build health 🛠️
Startup and sign-in flows are more resilient: unreadable configs can be healed and explained, transient store reads won’t reset profiles, and session expiry remains classifiable. Desktop packaging got targeted fixes (AppImage paths, userns relaxation, D‑Bus session bus), Tauri window behavior is improved for mixed-DPI multi-monitor setups, and CI/test coverage/stability got meaningful upgrades.

([#4716](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4716), [#4772](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4772), [#5081](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5081), [#5083](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5083), [#5171](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5171), [#5181](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5181), [#5189](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5189), [#5190](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5190), [#5221](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5221), [#5241](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5241), [#5252](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5252), [#5255](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5255), [#5267](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5267), [#5276](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5276), [#5277](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5277), [#5311](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5311), [#5336](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5336), [#5337](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5337), [#5340](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5340), [#5341](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5341)) — Thank you @YellowSnnowmann, @senamakel, @M3gA-Mind, @samrusani, @myi1, and @senamakel!

### Medulla, SDK routing, and backend-facing plumbing 🌐
OpenHuman is increasingly positioned as the Medulla core, with new facades/RPC surfaces and workflow-plane serving to the hosted orchestrator. The backend client is now routed through a vendored tinyhumans SDK, managed backend traffic is cut over, and several Medulla/MCP catalog and URL-resolution fixes help keep things consistent end-to-end.

# The Composio Reliability Upgrade

This patch release tightens up Composio task execution and makes tool-calls more resilient, so your agents can get to work faster and recover more gracefully when model output gets messy. 🚀

## Highlights

### Composio task execution & schema validation 🧩
Composio actions triggered via `integrations_agent` now avoid a frustrating “first call bounce” and can execute immediately when the model’s arguments already match the resolved live contract. This prevents loops like “fetch my latest email” stalling before `GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS` ever runs, especially along the text-mode per-action path. ([#5132](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5132)) — Thank you @M3gA-Mind!

### Tool-call parsing robustness (Kimi recovery) 🛠️
Tool-call parsing has been hardened to better recover from Kimi-K2-family garbled tool-call bodies. The normalization now strips the `<|\"|>` argument-quote sentinels and rewrites malformed `NAME{unquoted-json}` into a canonical form, improving resilience when model output is slightly corrupted. ([#5132](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5132)) — Thank you @M3gA-Mind!

Thanks to everyone who contributed to v0.63.1: @M3gA-Mind and @github-actions[bot].

body:
# The Reliability & Control Upgrade

This release is packed with sturdier workflows, smoother chat and Agent World experiences, and a ton of under-the-hood hardening to keep everything fast and dependable. 🎉

## Highlights

### Workflows you can trust 🧩
The Workflows copilot and canvas got a major reliability pass: proposals consistently render (even for larger graphs), every copilot turn now ends in a real terminal outcome (no more silent trail‑offs), Accept now saves automatically, and the runs UI stays accurate and live-updating. Safety and correctness also improved with fixes for live-arming on updates, better circuit-breaking, approval-state visibility, and stronger tier/approval enforcement for Composio tool calls.

([#4881](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4881), [#4886](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4886), [#4887](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4887), [#4888](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4888), [#4889](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4889), [#4890](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4890), [#4891](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4891), [#4893](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4893), [#4904](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4904), [#4911](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4911), [#4932](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4932), [#4933](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4933), [#4941](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4941), [#4942](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4942), [#4943](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4943), [#4945](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4945), [#4955](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4955), [#4956](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4956), [#4999](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4999), [#5000](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5000), [#5007](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5007), [#5011](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5011), [#5012](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5012), [#5013](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5013)) — Thank you @graycyrus and @senamakel!

### Chat that feels snappier & more controllable 💬
Chat got a big UX win with a Stop button plus ESC-to-interrupt and re-edit, and stronger protection against “hydrate” snapshots wiping fresh streaming or tool timelines. Orchestration also became more transparent: async sub-agent failures and “awaiting user” outcomes now surface correctly in chat, and delegations are now async-by-default with durable, resumable sessions and persistent workflow proposals.

([#4898](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4898), [#4903](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4903), [#4908](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4908), [#5074](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5074)) — Thank you @M3gA-Mind, @graycyrus, and @senamakel!

### Memory & transcript upgrades 🧠
Memory ingestion and recall got sharper and safer: OpenHuman can ingest Codex and Claude coding sessions, Composio sync no longer keys upserts off secret-like titles, and recall avoids pulling same-session “echo” documents that drown out real facts. On top of that, transcripts are now much more robust: cold-boot resumes restore full-fidelity context and thinking, and the transcript system is moving to an append-only, derived view with raw session logs as the source of truth.

([#4863](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4863), [#4953](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4953), [#4991](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4991), [#5077](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5077), [#5086](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5086)) — Thank you @senamakel, @M3gA-Mind, and @graycyrus!

### Agent World (Tiny Place) feels alive 🌍
Tiny Place is now more interactive and complete: DMs and feeds update in real time, ledgers and feeds paginate beyond the first 50 items, and directory entries finally open a rich profile view. Profiles also leveled up with editing for your own profile (name/bio/avatar) and a public viewer route for arbitrary handles.

([#4951](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4951), [#4952](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4952), [#4988](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4988), [#4989](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4989), [#4990](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4990), [#4994](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4994), [#4996](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4996), [#4997](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4997)) — Thank you @M3gA-Mind!

### Performance, polish, and “it just works” fixes ⚡
From accessibility and UI polish to startup and runtime performance, this release reduces friction across the app: improved dark theme contrast, paused mesh-gradient rendering when the app isn’t visible, and boot polling is consolidated and quieter. First-run setup overlays now appear only when actually provisioning, channel setup guidance is corrected in-app, pricing/checkout redirects behave properly, and the settings “Clear App Data” reset now correctly targets the signed-in user.

([#4897](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4897), [#4902](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4902), [#4905](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4905), [#4910](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4910), [#4939](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4939), [#4954](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4954), [#5035](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5035), [#5036](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5036), [#5066](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5066), [#5075](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5075), [#5085](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5085)) — Thank you @M3gA-Mind, @YellowSnnowmann, and @senamakel!

### Build flexibility, CI hardening, and new surfaces 🛠️
The core is now far more modular and easier to ship in slim builds via compile-time feature gates (media, web3, flows, skills, MCP, meet) and a new feature-gated terminal chat UI (`openhuman tui`). Desktop shipping and CI also got stricter and safer: voice and tokenjuice-treesitter are correctly forwarded into the desktop build, CI now gates feature-forwarding drift, macOS clippy blockers are resolved, the “gates-off” smoke lane is repaired and runs tests, and learning startup subscribers are decoupled from channels and covered with more stable tests. There’s also a core refactor moving the web chat conduit out of `channels/`.

([#4840](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4840), [#4855](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4855), [#4912](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4912), [#4913](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4913), [#4914](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4914), [#4915](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4915), [#4916](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4916), [#4917](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4917), [#4934](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4934), [#5004](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5004), [#5020](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5020), [#5023](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5023), [#5025](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5025), [#5070](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5070), [#5082](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5082), [#5084](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5084)) — Thank you @oxoxDev, @CodeGhost21, @senamakel, and @M3gA-Mind!

### Integrations, inference, and tooling improvements 🔌
Integrations and local AI got more reliable: OpenAI-compatible local runtimes now probe `/v1/models` correctly, custom embedding endpoint verification errors are clearer and actionable, and streaming retries now honor `Retry-After`. Composio tool execution is smarter and safer with per-action tools gated on their full contracts (reducing argument guessing), and unsyncable toolkits no longer auto-register as memory sources. There’s also a new `generate_document` tool that emits real `.docx`, plus a public accessor for last-turn usage totals for downstream hosting/billing.

([#4899](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4899), [#4909](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4909), [#4940](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4940), [#4993](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4993), [#4995](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4995), [#5064](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5064), [#5067](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5067)) — Thank you @M3gA-Mind and @senamakel!

### Account, sharing, and navigation delights 🔗
You can now generate one-tap “look what my agent did” share cards for X and LinkedIn, the X/Twitter “Continue with Google” popup stays in-app, Rewards is finally discoverable via a cloud-gated sidebar entry, and the Codex auth button is properly localized. Plus: proactive “Agentic task insights” fixtures and lifecycle resets were tightened to keep the UI consistent.

([#4892](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4892), [#4944](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4944), [#4949](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4949), [#4992](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4992), [#5010](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5010), [#5015](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5015), [#5065](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5065)) — Thank you @YellowSnnowmann, @graycyrus, and @M3gA-Mind!

### Safety & prompt discipline changes 🧯
Desktop automation safety controls saw churn: an Emergency Stop was introduced and later fully removed based on product direction. Meanwhile, agent behavior improved for local LLM providers with provider-aware context/delegation guardrails, stronger structured-output enforcement, more resilient tool-call parsing for small models, and AGENTS.md instructions are now loaded into the system prompt—with follow-up security hardening to prevent symlink/path escape and to redact debug logs when AGENTS.md is present.

([#4600](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4600), [#4900](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4900), [#4935](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4935), [#4938](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4938), [#5073](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5073), [#5087](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5087), [#5096](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/5096)) — Thank you @CodeGhost21, @M3gA-Mind, @sanil-23, @yh928, and @senamakel!

body:
# The Meetings & Connections Power‑Up

v0.58.0–v0.58.7 is packed with a sharper Meetings experience, faster + more reliable Connections (Skills/MCP), and a big wave of stability upgrades across agents, memory, and providers. 🚀

## Highlights

### Meetings, end-to-end polish 🎥
Meetings got a full redesign with a platform selector, a clean history master-detail layout, and smarter defaults—plus a bunch of quality fixes that make sessions feel more “alive” and less error-prone. You’ll see better UI feedback (including “Leaving…” states), automatic refresh of Recent Calls when a meeting ends, and improved handling of backend capacity messaging.

Wake phrases are now correctly forwarded for active meeting bots, meeting display names can auto-fill from your connected account, and the auto-summarize policy is honored—with a new manual summary RPC for “Ask” flows.  
([#4308](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4308), [#4348](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4348), [#4347](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4347), [#4221](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4221), [#4231](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4231), [#4297](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4297), [#4353](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4353)) — Thank you @graycyrus and @YOMXXX!

### Connections: MCP & Skills that feel fast (and stay fast) 🔌
MCP took a major leap forward: the MCP Servers page is now “complete” with a curated catalog, lifecycle improvements, and E2E coverage. Under the hood, MCP tool calls return as soon as the reply frame arrives (huge latency win), stdio servers spawn with the user’s real shell `PATH` (hello `npx`/`uvx`), and schema migrations are now concurrency-safe.

Auth and install UX also improved across the board: clearer MCP 401 explanations (with safer messaging), better “installed / installing” card state, and Skills improvements like activation persistence, registry caching + pagination, and latency instrumentation.  
([#4300](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4300), [#4220](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4220), [#4295](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4295), [#4219](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4219), [#4321](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4321), [#4224](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4224), [#4288](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4288), [#4120](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4120), [#4182](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4182), [#4188](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4188), [#4238](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4238)) — Thank you @YellowSnnowmann, @M3gA-Mind, @oxoxDev, and @YOMXXX!

### Chat experience: attachments, visuals, and smoother long turns 💬
Chat now has a first-class attachment button for images, videos, and documents—with drag-and-drop and paste support. Code blocks gained syntax highlighting across markdown surfaces, and the composer/footer layout now dynamically reserves space so queued follow-ups (and other expanding footer content) no longer overlap the conversation.

On the reliability side, long reasoning turns stay alive past the old 2-minute silence timeout thanks to a heartbeat progress signal.  
([#4292](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4292), [#4335](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4335), [#4334](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4334), [#4282](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4282)) — Thank you @oxoxDev and @graycyrus!

### Agents & tool runtime: fewer loops, clearer stops 🧠
Agent orchestration is now much harder to derail: identical tool-call loops are detected and halted, stuck sub-agents can return as explicitly *incomplete*, and session tool calls now respect timeouts instead of hanging forever. The MCP Setup Agent no longer gets trapped in a re-spawn loop when pausing for user clarification, and goal completion instructions were strengthened to improve auto-complete behavior.

The built-in researcher agent was also tightened up with a bounded tool surface and capped per-turn output.  
([#4230](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4230), [#4262](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4262), [#4303](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4303), [#4310](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4310), [#4313](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4313), [#4314](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4314)) — Thank you @sanil-23, @YOMXXX, @oxoxDev, @salarkhannn, and @senamakel!

### Memory & intelligence: better continuity and safer cross-host behavior 🗂️
Memory got meaningful durability upgrades: summary-only wiki history is now tracked via git, cross-thread search is faster by ranking before cloning heavy hits, and the Trees UI has clearer feedback and a stable toolbar layout even when vault guidance opens.

For multi-device setups, cross-host vault paths are now explicitly surfaced as belonging to a particular host OS—so a frontend won’t try to open macOS paths on Linux (or vice versa). The Brain memory graph reliably reloads after re-login, and the Intelligence page scrolls correctly inside the Brain card.  
([#4168](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4168), [#4311](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4311), [#4331](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4331), [#4342](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4342), [#4330](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4330), [#4223](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4223), [#4332](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4332)) — Thank you @senamakel, @mysma-9403, @graycyrus, @oxoxDev, and @M3gA-Mind!

### Provider, inference, and observability hardening 🧰
This release includes a broad set of fixes that turn noisy “errors” into correctly-classified expected states, reduce retry storms, and improve resilience across providers and local environments. Highlights include: safer model-catalog parsing, better embeddings verification (including auto-detected dimensions and Gemini model-id normalization), improved handling of quota/limit states, and more robust OpenAI-compat parsing.

Backend routing is also safer: backend API calls won’t accidentally route to a BYO cloud inference host. For channels, OAuth “Connecting” states now recover cleanly when deep-link roundtrips fail. And for cron jobs, missing API keys halt early (with better user-visible error surfacing).  
([#4157](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4157), [#4160](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4160), [#4184](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4184), [#4186](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4186), [#4185](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4185), [#4207](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4207), [#4209](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4209), [#4210](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4210), [#4161](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4161), [#4189](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4189), [#4187](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4187), [#4208](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4208), [#4286](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4286), [#4306](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4306), [#4166](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4166), [#4169](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4169)) — Thank you @oxoxDev and @M3gA-Mind!

### Tiny Place: identity + trading fixes, smoother Linux rendering 🪙
Tiny Place saw a strong round of fixes: correct pricing tiers, USDC SPL mint acceptance for handle registration, longer RPC timeouts for bounty creation, and a more polished UX for destructive actions via an in-app confirm modal. Trading is more usable too—balances are read from the correct settlement RPC, Buy re-enables properly after a purchase attempt, and users can switch their primary handle across multiple identities.

On Linux, the world renderer now gets a working WebGL context via SwiftShader (without reverting to the old “disable GPU” blunt instrument).  
([#4215](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4215), [#4211](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4211), [#4212](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4212), [#4214](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4214), [#4218](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4218), [#4217](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4217), [#4216](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4216), [#4213](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4213)) — Thank you @M3gA-Mind!

### Voice, Human, devices, and desktop reliability 🎙️
Voice on macOS is more robust: in-process Whisper STT can work without relying on an external binary, and the install/test UI behaves more predictably. Human UI also gets a practical fix: the mic device selector stays within the viewport instead of clipping off-screen.

Desktop reliability improvements include a CEF GPU-disable startup override for tough environments, Debian installs preferring `.deb` packages (with proper runtime deps), and device pairing now using the correct Socket.IO ACK flow.  
([#3915](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/3915), [#4343](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4343), [#4309](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4309), [#4263](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4263), [#4355](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4355)) — Thank you @YellowSnnowmann, @graycyrus, @Sam, and @YOMXXX!

### New creative tools, mascots, and model routing ✨
There’s a whole new media-generation domain with image/video agents and GMI media tools that download outputs into stable local paths. Mascots can now load from a GitHub-backed manifest, making it easier to expand and evolve the Human experience over time. On the routing side, the new `burst-v1` tier is registered and used for appropriate low-context workers, including the SuperContext scout and other tool-driving agents.

There’s also improved auditability for channel replies by recording provider/model metadata on processed channel events.  
([#4244](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4244), [#4312](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4312), [#4260](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4260), [#4315](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4315), [#3682](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/3682)) — Thank you @senamakel, @senamakel-droid, and @ron-liu!

### Smaller (but mighty) fixes across the stack 🛠️
A collection of sharp fixes landed across token accounting, learning, security, people, artifacts, and CI ergonomics. TokenJuice avoids UTF-8 char-boundary panics and correctly attributes compaction savings to the per-turn model; usage gauges no longer exceed 100% due to sub-agent tokens; learning stability uses the correct facet half-life; chat files hydrate from the artifact ledger on cold start; and the people store is correctly seeded at core boot.

Security hardening also tightened several untrusted-input sinks, and CI coverage runs are stabilized by raising `RUST_MIN_STACK` to avoid llvm-cov stack overflows.  
([#4170](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4170), [#4229](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4229), [#4327](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4327), [#4328](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4328), [#4232](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4232), [#4345](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4345), [#4158](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4158), [#4346](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4346)) — Thank you @mysma-9403, @rainbowpuffpuff, @oxoxDev, @Sam, @obchain, and @graycyrus!

### Documentation updates 📚
Docs received a substantial GitBook/README overhaul and a set of correctness follow-ups to tighten terminology, scope, and RPC naming.  
([#4225](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4225), [#4243](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4243)) — Thank you @senamakel!
### Additional highlights 🔗

A few more focused contributions round out this release with targeted fixes and improvements that are worth calling out. ([#4140](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4140), [#4163](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4163), [#4183](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4183), [#4287](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4287), [#4293](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4293), [#4296](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4296), [#4318](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4318)) — Thank you @senamakel-droid, @oxoxDev, @M3gA-Mind, @YellowSnnowmann, and @YOMXXX!

## New Contributors

- Thank you @rainbowpuffpuff for fixing TokenJuice savings attribution so compaction savings are credited to the per-turn model. ([#4229](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4229))
- Thank you @salarkhannn for strengthening the goal completion directive to improve agent auto-complete behavior. ([#4310](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openhuman/pull/4310))
